thread_analysis.thread_summary: Alps Alpine (contact Tsutomu Nitta, DS Planning Dept.) works with Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Jun Wang, Masaya Iida) on Bluetooth SIG certification for three OEM/ODM-manufactured products (an integrated module, a vital sensor, and a location beacon) built around Nordic and Telink SoCs sourced from an external Chinese manufacturer. The thread documents an extensive technical negotiation spanning August-November 2024: RF PHY test lab accreditation requirements, the formal test-exemption boundary for already-registered SoCs versus the brand owner's own quality-assurance interest, quote-form field semantics under the new registration system, a GAP/Isochronous cross-layer inconsistency resolved via an earlier Host Subsystem version, the SoC-vs-module distinction for RF test reuse eligibility (with a Gerber-data-based antenna-circuit-similarity test-reduction alternative), and scoping RF PHY test coverage to actual deployment usage rather than full chip-level theoretical capability.
all_questions_found: Must RF PHY test data come from an accredited lab, and does the report need our company's name? (see thread_0275_case_01)
Can non-accredited results become usable with Allion's review, and is RF PHY testing formally required for an already-registered SoC? (see thread_0275_case_02)
What should be written in the renamed 'Profiles' field on the quote request form? (see thread_0275_case_03)
How can a GAP/Isochronous cross-layer Consistency Check inconsistency between Controller and Host Subsystem versions be resolved without triggering GAP testing? (see thread_0275_case_04)
Does the module-vendor RF test exemption apply to bare SoC implementations, and can RF PHY testing be reduced across products sharing the same SoC? (see thread_0275_case_05)
Does theoretical chip-level multi-mode PHY support require testing all modes even if real communication partners only use one mode? (see thread_0275_case_06)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread provides a comprehensive view of multi-product OEM/ODM certification coordination: test-evidence accreditation requirements, the distinction between formal registration exemptions and brand-owner quality assurance interests, registration-site field semantics evolving under the new system, a creative cross-layer-inconsistency resolution via an earlier vendor-registered Host Subsystem version, the SoC-vs-module eligibility boundary for test-reuse exemptions (with a Gerber-data-verified antenna-circuit-similarity alternative), and grounding RF PHY test scope in actual deployment usage rather than theoretical chip capability.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See the individual case files (thread_0275_case_01 through thread_0275_case_06) for the decision logic behind each question.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0275_case_01 through thread_0275_case_06 for the specific risks of each question.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion consistently ran preliminary trial-project Consistency Checks ahead of customer commitment (catching the GAP/Isochronous issue early) and proactively distinguished formal exemptions from quality-assurance best practices rather than letting the customer assume formal exemption meant testing was unnecessary altogether.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For multi-product OEM/ODM certification engagements involving externally-manufactured SoC-based products, proactively verify test lab accreditation, distinguish formal registration requirements from brand-owner quality assurance interests, run preliminary Consistency Checks to catch cross-layer inconsistencies before customer commitment, and scope RF PHY testing to actual deployment usage (with Gerber-data-verified antenna-circuit similarity as a path to reduce duplicate testing across same-SoC products) rather than full theoretical chip capability.
